title: Inquest called into death of man in police custody
article: A mandatory coroner's inquest will look into the circumstances of the death of Christopher Coffey, who died at the Southampton hospital more than a year ago after a struggle with police.
The Special Investigations Unit, a police oversight agency, found no reason to charge Saugeen Shores Police Service officers in relation to Coffey's death, which occurred June 21, 2013.

Dr. Rick Mann, the supervising coroner in this area, issued a news release Wednesday to announce the inquest into the 46-year-old's death. It is expected to take five days and begin Dec. 1, the release said. Dr. Thomas Wilson will preside and Vanessa Decker will be the coroner's counsel. Fifteen witnesses are expected to be called.
A jury may recommend how to prevent similar deaths.
The SIU and Saugeen Shores police have described the events surrounding Coffey's death while he was in police custody.
According to Saugeen Shores police, just before 11 p.m. on June 21, 2013, officers were dispatched to a Port Elgin residence in response to a home invasion in progress.
A man had kicked in the front door of a residence on Oakwood Dr. A man living there fought with the intruder, who turned out to be Coffey, until police arrived.
The officers and the man struggled with the intruder untuil he was handcuffed. It was then noticed the man was not breathing and he had no vital signs.
The handcuffs were removed, CPR was started and paramedics were called. The man was taken to Southampton hospital where he was pronounced dead, Saugeen Shores police said.

A pathologist concluded Coffey's death was associated with excited delirium and prone restraint, a SIU news release said. The SIU concluded police used no more force than necessary in the circumstances in which Coffey was experiencing "an acute manic episode".
According to eyewitnesses, none of the officers struck the man or used any of their weapons.
